summary: Added a default per-processor image count safety limit of 5, an InternVL override of 12, precedence for the existing --limit-mm-data-per-request server argument, early base-loader rejection, and common serving-dispatch validation for processors that bypass the base loader. Invalid configured limits now fail during server argument validation.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: the recorded base had no processor image-count default.

20 tests and 26 subtests covering default and processor-specific limits, exact boundaries, lower/higher/zero server overrides, unrelated modality overrides, preprocessed inputs, malformed values, rejection before decode, common serving dispatch, and existing media error classification.
Repository formatting, lint, spelling, AST, registry, and policy hooks for all changed source and test files.

gpu_execution_evidence: The feature is a CPU-side request-count validation guard that rejects before image fetch/decode or model execution. No numerical kernel or model output changes were made, so a GPU numerical reference was not applicable.
remaining_limitations: No model-weight HTTP server run was performed: the deterministic tiny Llama fixture is text-only and cannot qualify multimodal image processing, while the validation behavior is covered at the actual common serving dispatch and processor loader boundaries.

Only InternVL has a known architecture-specific override (12); all other current processors inherit the requested default of 5. Architecture-specific higher limits were not asserted without model-owner evidence.

Calls made directly to a custom processor's process_mm_data_async method outside SGLang's serving dispatch are protected only when that processor uses BaseMultimodalProcessor.load_mm_data; the supported serving path validates every registered processor before dispatch.
No native rebuild was applicable because all changes are Python request validation and tests; no FlyDSL, C++, compiler, ISA, Torch, or ROCm component changed.
